land.text: the South Caucasus lands of Nader Shah's empire, where 'semi-independent khanates emerged as a result of the lack of a centralized government' after his assassination in 1747

predecessors.note: Cliopatria lists Afsharid Iran as a neighbour in 1748-1756.

land.text: the khanates north of the Aras, 'forced ... into submission' by Agha Mohammad Khan in 1795 and crowned Shah in 1796; Cliopatria's Qajar shape reaches 41.98 N from 1797

successors.note: An aggregate row: the Khanates page says the individual khanates survived as Iranian dependencies until the Russians annexed them one by one, 1804-1828, which this dossier does not draw (see notes).

capitals.name: No single capital (aggregate of khanates; point is the centroid of the 1748 shape)
capitals.note: The page names no capital for the group; it gives only Lankaran as the seat of the Talysh Khanate.

keyframe_review.note: 88,036 km2. The page has no infobox area, so there is nothing to compare. The shape (43.6-50.3 E, 38.9-42.0 N; Azerbaijan, Armenia and the southern edge of Dagestan) fits the page's list of khanates 'that soon emerged after the death of Nader Shah in 1747': Baku, Derbent, Erivan, Ganja, Javad, Karabakh, Nakhchivan, Quba, Shaki, Shirvan and Talysh. Cliopatria's Seshat id is az_caucasus_khanates: this is an aggregate row, not one state.

87,987 km2, 48 km2 less than 1748-1762; no page opened records a change in 1763 (Karim Khan Zand ruled Iran 1751-1779 per the Zand page, and 'some khanates' coined in his name per the Khanates page), so the shape stands.

UNVERIFIED: page budget. 194,383 km2 for 1788-1790, twice the 1787 shape: it reaches 36.2 N, i.e. north-western Iran (Tabriz, Urmia, Zanjan). The Khanates page lists only South Caucasus khanates, none south of the Aras, and none of the five pages opened (Khanates, Zand dynasty, Karim Khan Zand, Agha Mohammad Khan, Persian expedition of 1796) mentions Azerbaijani Iran in 1788-1790. The Zand shape loses its northern third in 1788 and the Qajar shape takes it in 1791, so the addition is probably Cliopatria's placing of Iranian Azerbaijan between the two. A gap-filler should open the Urmia, Tabriz and Khoy khanate pages.
87,987 km2, identical to the 1763 shape: the khanates south of the Greater Caucasus and north of the Aras, as the page lists them. The Iranian addition of 1788-1790 is gone.

correction.text: the khanates as in 1791-1795: in 1796 they were still there, invaded by Zubov's army from April ('Russian troops set out from Kizlyar in April 1796') and by Agha Mohammad Khan's pressure, and not yet annexed by anyone

keyframe_review.note: 48 km2 near 44.3 E 40.7 N is a residue smaller than one grid cell (data/README.md, 'Shapes with tiny area'); it is not the khanates. The Persian expedition page has Russian troops overrunning 'most of the territory of modern-day Azerbaijan' by mid-June 1796, so the khanates' land was still there in 1796; use the 1791 shape for the year. Cliopatria's Qajar shape of 1796 (to 41.0 N) overlaps its southern half.

region.text: the khanates of the South Caucasus that 'soon emerged after the death of Nader Shah in 1747'

ledger.note: 1748: after Nader Shah's assassination in 1747 'semi-independent khanates emerged' across the South Caucasus. The page dates the cause (1747) and the list, not each khanate's founding; 1748 is Cliopatria's first year.

region.text: north-western Iran (to 36.2 N) added to the khanates' shape in 1788

ledger.note: 1788: page silent. Cliopatria adds about 106,000 km2 of Iranian Azerbaijan to the khanates as the Zand shape shrinks; no page opened dates or confirms it, and the Khanates page lists none south of the Aras.

region.text: north-western Iran, returned in the 1791 shape

ledger.note: 1791: Agha Mohammad Khan 'marched into Azerbaijan in the spring of 1791': he sent Soleyman Khan Qajar 'to make the Talysh Khanate acknowledge Qajar authority', 'forced the Sarab Khanate into submission', 'subdued the Ardabil Khanate' and 'appointed the Donboli noble Hosayn Qoli Donboli as the governor of Khoy and Tabriz'. The 1788 addition south of the Aras drops out of the 1791 shape and the Qajar shape grows to 39.8 N. Reviewer eu-19-f: raised from confidence 1 and re-sourced; the note said no page opened dated this, but the Agha Mohammad Khan page does.

region.text: the khanates north of the Aras that Agha Mohammad Khan set out to reassert Iranian rule over: 'Karabakh, Ganja, Shirvan' and the rest of the semi-independent khanates

ledger.note: 1795: Agha Mohammad Khan invades. 'In May 1795, Agha Mohammad Khan set out for Azerbaijan with an army of 60,000 cavalry and infantry'; Shusha was besieged 8 July-9 August, Ibrahim Khalil Khan of Karabakh submitted with hostages, Javad Khan of Ganja submitted, Quba was subdued, and Tbilisi was sacked on 11 September.

region.text: the khanates north of the Aras that Agha Mohammad Khan set out to reassert Iranian rule over: 'Karabakh, Ganja, Shirvan' and the rest of the semi-independent khanates

ledger.note: 1796: Agha Mohammad Khan is 'formally crowned in 1796' on the Mughan plain after wintering there; the page says he 'forced the local khanates into submission' (Karabakh, Ganja, Quba named). The year of the end of the contest is my reading of the coronation.

region.text: the khanates north of the Aras, submitted to Agha Mohammad Khan in 1795-96

ledger.note: 1796: the khanates pass under Qajar rule. The year is Cliopatria's row end and the page's coronation; the Khanates page has the individual khanates continuing as Iranian dependencies until Russian annexation (Talysh protectorate 1802, Ganja annexed 1804, Baku and Derbent 1806, Erivan and Nakhichevan 1828), so the dissolution is of the aggregate, not of each khanate.

region.text: Derbent, stormed on 10 May, and 'most of the territory of modern-day Azerbaijan, including three principal cities' (Baku, Shemakha, Ganja) by mid-June

ledger.note: 1796: Zubov's Russian army storms Derbent on 10 May 1796 and overruns the khanates by mid-June 'without any resistance'. The Agha Mohammad page adds that the Russians 'briefly took and occupied Derbent and Baku'.

region.text: the khanates overrun by Zubov, abandoned when Paul I 'ordered the withdrawal of all Russian troops from the region' after the Empress died in November 1796

ledger.note: 1796: Russia withdraws. The page gives the month of Catherine II's death (November) and Paul's order, not the day of the pull-out.

wars.name: Agha Mohammad Khan's campaign in the South Caucasus

zones.text: the khanates north of the Aras that Agha Mohammad Khan set out to reassert Iranian rule over: 'Karabakh, Ganja, Shirvan' and the rest of the semi-independent khanates

wars.outcome: Karabakh, Ganja and Quba submitted; Tbilisi was sacked on 11 September 1795 and the army pillaged Karabakh and Shirvan; Agha Mohammad was crowned in 1796. He was assassinated at Shusha in 1797 on a second campaign (outside this dossier).
wars.note: The page does not use 'vassal' or 'subjugated'; it says he 'forced the local khanates into submission'. Shusha was not entered.

wars.name: Persian expedition of 1796

zones.text: 'most of the territory of modern-day Azerbaijan, including three principal cities'

wars.outcome: Russian victory on the field: Derbent stormed 10 May, Baku, Shemakha and Ganja overrun by mid-June; Paul I ordered the withdrawal after Catherine II's death in November 1796. The infobox lists no territorial change.
wars.note: Infobox belligerents: Russia, Kartli-Kakheti and Imereti against Qajar Iran, the Ganja and Erivan khanates.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line separates the khanates from Iran, Georgia, the Ottomans or one another in these years; the outline follows Cliopatria.

notes:
Aggregate row: Cliopatria's 'Khanates of the Caucasus' (Seshat id az_caucasus_khanates) lumps independent khanates; the data README lists it among the aggregates carried as leaf polities. Typed 'state' here so the land is drawn; the individual khanates (Karabakh, Ganja, Shirvan, Quba, Baku, Shaki, Talysh, Erivan, Nakhichevan, Derbent, Javad) have no dossier from this batch and need one from eu-19-x if the map is to show them separately.
End year: the dossier ends in 1796 with Cliopatria, whose Qajar shape covers the land from 1797. The Khanates page itself dates the khanates' ends to Russian annexations (Talysh protectorate 1802, Ganja 1804, Javad 1805 into Shirvan, Karabakh/Quba/Shaki/Shirvan protectorates 1805 and abolitions 1822/1816/1819/1820, Baku and Derbent 1806, Erivan and Nakhichevan 1827-28): they were Qajar dependencies for 1797-1804 and later Russian possessions. Those events belong to the russian-empire and qajar-dynasty dossiers (vassal and gain events with the khanates as counterparts).
Unverified: the 1788-1790 Iranian addition (see the 1788 keyframe); the pages opened did not cover it. The 1796 shape is a sub-cell residue (verdict wrong). Karim Khan Zand's overlordship (1751-1779) of 'some of the Caucasian lands' is undated on both Zand pages opened, so no vassal event is written.
Page budget: 5 of 5 used, two of them (Zand dynasty, Karim Khan Zand) nearly empty on the topic.
Counterparts: afsharid-iran, zand-dynasty, qajar-dynasty (me-10); russian-empire (eu-17); kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti (eu-19).
